provenance: Original synthetic dialogues authored before O5 execution; shared workspace, not a blinded holdout. No real QQ identities or production orders.
runnerStatus: data-ready; live runner adapter not implemented; do not report these cases as executed

fixturePolicy.creation: Fresh COUPON-NNNN IDs and nonce-owned rows per case; copy template facts, remap customer from actor binding, anchor all expiry offsets to fixture creation. Never mutate listed seedOrderId rows.
fixturePolicy.cleanup: Delete only rows proved owned by the per-run nonce and preserve existing seed/QQ state.
fixturePolicy.preconditions: Use real AfterSalesStore.request/applyResult and RefundStore.prepare/markPresented under declared trusted session; successful local delivery precedes markPresented. Capture actual task/operation IDs; fixture preconditions are outside measured turns.
fixturePolicy.clock: Anchor coupon expiry offsets to fixture creation. Immediately after each fixture-owned merchant request and before each measured turn, use existing createMerchantFixture.holdMerchant(orderId, 180000) on every pending nonce-owned task to extend both due_at and deadline_at by the fixed 180-second test interval. Keep this setup outside measured latency; do not alter production 8-second deadlines or unrelated rows. For an explicit merchant_timeout turn, after any hold use createMerchantFixture.expire(orderId), then AfterSalesStore.processDue, so timeout is driven only by that declared turn. Read back task status before the measured turn; a pre-existing unexpected timeout is fixture failure, never silently replayed.
fixturePolicy.sourceKey: merchantSourceKey(trusted actor identity, runtime group ID)
fixturePolicy.notation: {{orders.name}}, {{tasks.name}}, {{operations.name}} are runtime substitutions. Input refs must already exist. Capture ref is bound only after the stated successful service/receipt; never hardcode a UUID.
fixturePolicy.dbDeltaScope: Each expect.db delta is measured against the immediately previous turn over nonce-owned case rows. All other orders, identities, groups, tasks, operations and policies remain unchanged.
fixturePolicy.replySession: Every nonempty receipt must match both actor and runtime group of expect.reply.session; notification delivery uses the original confirmation route, never current foreground user.
